al-Qasim said: We counted, and it came to exactly a thousand months, neither more by a day nor less by a day. The one meant by al-Qasim is al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl, who is mentioned in its chain of narration.

al-Tirmidhi said: This Yusuf is unknown, meaning Yusuf ibn Sa'd, who narrated it from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali.

Ibn Kathir said: There is room for examination in this, for a group of people narrated from him, including Hammad ibn Salama, Khalid al-Hadhdha' and Yunus ibn 'Ubayd.

Yahya ibn Ma'in said about him: He is well-known (mashhur).

In another report from Ibn Ma'in, he said: He is trustworthy (thiqa). Ibn Jarir narrated it through the route of al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl from 'Isa ibn Mazin.

Ibn Kathir said: Then this hadith, under every assessment, is extremely munkar (rejected).

al-Mizzi said: It is a munkar hadith. And the statement of al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl that he calculated the duration of the Banu Umayya and found it to be exactly a thousand months, neither more nor less, is not correct, for the total of their period from the time Mu'awiya alone took power, which was the year forty (AH), until the Banu al-'Abbas stripped them of power, which was the year one hundred and thirty-two (AH), totals ninety-two years.

al-Khatib narrated in his History from Ibn 'Abbas something similar to what was narrated from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali.

al-Khatib narrated from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, as a mursal report traced to the Prophet ﷺ, something similar to it.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿Salam﴾, that he said: On that night the rebellious devils are chained, the powerful jinn are shackled, all the gates of heaven are opened, and Allah accepts repentance from every penitent on it. Therefore He said: ﴿Salamun hiya hatta matla'i al-fajr﴾. He said: That is from the setting of the sun until the rising of dawn. The hadiths on the excellence of the Night of Power are numerous, and this is not the place to expound them; likewise the hadiths on identifying it and the disagreement concerning that.
